title: Cutscene manifest
description: A cutscene is a manifest, not a script: an opaque engine asset key plus the game-state effects applied when it completes. Motion, camera, and timing live in the engine's own timeline tooling — never in JSON. Chain staging→talk→staging via entersDialogue + play_cutscene effects; no dialogue nests inside a cutscene.

asset.description: Opaque key to an engine asset (e.g. 'Cutscenes/HarbourArrival'). Parlance never resolves it — a mismatch is the engine loader's error to report, not Parlance's.

skippable.description: Player may skip; skipping applies effectsOnComplete immediately.

effectsOnComplete.description: The only game-state a cutscene produces, applied when it ends.

entersDialogue.description: Chain: dialogue to open when the cutscene finishes.

arrivesAt.description: Where the player stands when this cutscene ends. Applied by the host after effectsOnComplete and after clearing pendingCutscene, before entersDialogue. Any motion inside the cutscene is choreography only: skipping and watching in full must land in the same place with the same state. Omit for a cutscene that plays in place.
